references.text: Balak, son of Zippor, was the king of Moab who feared Israel after their victory over the Amorites and tried to get Balaam to curse them.
The background for Jephthah's argument: Israel camped on the plains of Moab after defeating the Amorites.
Balak complained to Balaam because he blessed Israel instead of cursing them, but he never fought against Israel.
Balak was angry with Balaam but sent him home without attacking Israel militarily.
Moses reminds Israel that Balak, son of Zippor, tried to use Balaam against them, but God turned the curse into a blessing.
Joshua reminds the people that Balak fought against Israel, but God delivered them.
The prophet Micah reminds the people of Balak's plans and Balaam's response to show God's righteous deeds.
